To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) mid-level features for recognition can be obtained from a combination of hard vector quantization and max pooling; (ii) soft vector quantization and sparse coding are not necessary; (iii) the best performing sparse coding scheme can be improved by learning a discriminative dictionary; (iv) the max pooling operation has a natural interpretation as the winner-takes-all operation of a neural network with rectified linear units

(1) max pooling is the most effective pooling scheme, (2) hard vector quantization is the most effective coding scheme, (3) supervised discriminative sparse coding is a promising coding scheme, and (4) max pooling is a good way to combine the features from different coding schemes.

1) the combination of hard vector quantization and max pooling is a very competitive baseline for mid level feature extraction; 2) sparse coding with a discriminative dictionary is an effective coding scheme that outperforms the baseline on all the datasets; and 3) the max pooling scheme is very effective, and can be explained in terms of a probabilistic model.
